Expectation1: Design and develop technical solutions to meet project requirements
Situation1: Stakeholders expect a working prototype soon to secure internal approval
Expectation2: Support individuals or groups in accessing essential services and resources
Situation2: They encounter a situation where someone urgently needs housing, medical help, or protection and must be connected to services quickly.
Story: I sat at my desk, blueprints spread out before me, the hum of the office a constant reminder of the looming deadline. As an engineer, I was expected to deliver a working prototype by the end of the week—stakeholders were anxious, their emails growing more insistent. The project’s future, and perhaps my own, hinged on this. Yet, my phone buzzed with a message from the shelter: a young woman needed immediate help—she had nowhere to sleep tonight and was in desperate need of medical attention. As an advocate, I was her lifeline, the one who could connect her to the right services before it was too late. My mind raced, torn between the technical challenges on my screen and the urgent human need in my inbox. Each role demanded my full attention, but I only had one self to give. The weight of expectation pressed down, and I felt myself pulled in two directions, heart pounding as I tried to decide which call to answer first.
